title: Console backend: Audit Logs API (filtering, pagination, RBAC enforcement + rate limiting)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Goal
Ship an enterprise-ready Audit Logs API in the Console backend to support the Console “Audit Logs” page and audit log export workflows. API must support filtering + stable pagination, enforce RBAC, and include performance and rate limiting guardrails.

Context
This is part of the audit log program to standardize schema v1 and reach 100% coverage for sensitive actions. Enterprise customers are blocked on being able to query audit events in-product and export them reliably.

Scope
1) Read API (list/query)
- Endpoint: GET /console/v1/audit-logs
- Required: org-scoped only (no cross-org access)
- Filtering (all optional unless noted):
  - time range: start_time (required) + end_time (required); default end_time=now; max window 31 days
  - event_name (exact match; allow multiple)
  - outcome (success|failure)
  - actor_id (exact match)
  - actor_type (user|service|system)
  - target_type + target_id (exact match)
  - request_id (exact match)
  - ip (exact match; admin-only field exposure, see “Field-level access”)
- Pagination:
  - Cursor-based pagination (opaque cursor)
  - sort order fixed: occurred_at DESC, then event_id DESC for tie-break
  - limit default 50, max 200
- Response includes:
  - events[] in schema v1 envelope as stored (with redactions applied)
  - next_cursor (if more results)
  - request_id echoed for client correlation

2) Export API (async job)
- Endpoint: POST /console/v1/audit-logs/exports
- Creates an export job that generates a signed download URL or pushes to configured sink (phase 1 is “download from console”; sinks handled by exporter service workstream).
- Filters reuse same shape as list/query.
- Enforce stricter limits:
  - max window 7 days per export job
  - max events per export (soft limit) with partial export error semantics
- Endpoint: GET /console/v1/audit-logs/exports/:id (status)

3) RBAC + permissions
- Enforce explicit permissions (do not rely on “org admin” boolean):
  - audit_logs.read for GET /audit-logs
  - audit_logs.export for POST /audit-logs/exports and GET /exports/:id
- Ensure permissions are present in RBAC policy bundle defaults and migration notes (coordinate with policy bundle PR).
- Actor attribution: Audit Logs API accesses must themselves generate audit events (read/export) with actor identity and query parameters (redacted). NOTE: “read of audit logs” is sensitive; must be logged.

4) Rate limiting + abuse controls
- Read/list endpoint:
  - per-org: 60 req/min (burst 120)
  - per-user: 30 req/min
- Export endpoint:
  - per-org: 5 exports/hour
  - per-user: 2 exports/hour
- Reject overly broad queries:
  - require time range; reject missing or >31 days
  - reject limit >200
  - reject queries with no time range and no indexed filters

5) Performance considerations
- Data store assumptions: audit events are stored in the audit-log pipeline store (queryable store; current implementation reads via internal AuditLogQueryService).
- Must be index-friendly:
  - required time range to leverage occurred_at partition/index
  - exact-match filters only (no full-text search in v1)
- Implement server-side “query plan guardrails”:
  - if request would scan >N partitions (e.g., >31 days), return 400 with actionable error
  - apply hard timeout (e.g., 2s) for list queries; return partial error with retry guidance
- Ensure response payload size is bounded:
  - cap event payload size per event (truncate + include “payload_truncated=true” marker in response metadata if needed)

6) Field-level access + privacy
- Default response excludes high-risk fields unless caller has audit_logs.read_sensitive_fields:
  - ip address
  - user_agent
- Ensure payload redaction rules are applied consistently (no secrets/tokens). If store is already redacted, still enforce a final “belt and suspenders” scrubber in the API layer.

Error semantics
- 401 unauthenticated
- 403 authenticated but missing permission
- 400 invalid filters (missing time range, window too large, unsupported filter combinations)
- 429 rate limited (include retry-after)
- 500/503 upstream query service issues

Acceptance criteria
- [x] GET /console/v1/audit-logs supports time-range + at least event_name/outcome/actor/target/request_id filters with cursor pagination
- [x] RBAC permissions enforced with unit tests
- [x] Read/export actions produce audit events with schema v1, including request_id correlation
- [x] Rate limiting is enabled with explicit per-org/per-user thresholds and 429 behavior verified
- [x] Performance guardrails: max window enforcement, limit cap, and query timeout
- [x] API documented in repo + linked from Confluence program docs

Non-goals / follow-ups
- Full-text search, regex filters, and arbitrary JSON payload queries (explicitly out of scope)
- Cross-org “super admin” search tooling (internal-only; separate ticket + access policy)
- SIEM sink exports via exporter service are tracked in exporter hardening workstream

Links
- Implementation PR: sources/github/redwood/pr_18520.json (Console backend Audit Logs API endpoints)
- RBAC permissions PR: sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr_97.json
- Related work:
  - ENG-2481 (schema v1)
  - ENG-2482 (shared lib/validator)
  - ENG-2489 (delivery lag SLO + dashboards)

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - permission matrix for read/export
  - filter validation (time window, limit cap)
  - cursor pagination stability
  - redaction enforcement (ip/user_agent gated)
- Integration tests (staging): covered by ENG-2492; ensure at least one test hits read/export endpoints and asserts audit events emitted for audit log access.

Rollout plan
- Ship behind feature flag: console.audit_logs_api.enabled
- Enable for internal orgs first, then beta design partners
- Monitor:
  - p95 latency for list queries
  - 429 rates
  - export job failure rates
  - audit events for audit_logs.read/export present and correctly permissioned
comments: 2025-06-03 (Chloe Martin): Started implementation in console-backend. Plan is to proxy reads through AuditLogQueryService instead of direct DB access to avoid duplicating query logic and to keep store auth centralized. Will add cursor encoding using (occurred_at,event_id) tuple.

2025-06-06 (Marcus Lin): RBAC needs to be explicit permission checks; please avoid “org_admin” shortcut. Also we need to audit access to audit logs (read + export). That audit event should NOT include raw query params like IP/user_agent; only include safe filter summary + time window.

2025-06-10 (Allison Grant): Please make sort order fixed and deterministic. For pagination, cursor should include both timestamp and unique id; do not use offset pagination. Add request_id propagation end-to-end so Security can correlate reads with upstream actions.

2025-06-13 (Chloe Martin): Added validation: start_time/end_time required; max 31d for list; max 7d for exports; limit max 200. Implemented rate limiting (org + user). Working through field-gating for ip/user_agent; will require audit_logs.read_sensitive_fields permission.

2025-06-18 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure list endpoint has a strict timeout (we’ve seen query service degrade during exporter backlog). Prefer returning 503 with retry-after rather than hanging requests; also emit metrics for query failures/timeouts.

2025-06-21 (Chloe Martin): PR up (18520). Includes endpoints, rate limits, and emits audit_logs.read + audit_logs.export_request events. Added response size caps to avoid huge payloads. Waiting on rbac-policy-bundle permission merge for audit_logs.*.

2025-06-24 (Naomi Feldman): Confirmed this unblocks DES-133 (UI) and PM beta criteria as long as export supports download (even before SIEM sinks). Please ensure docs mention the filter limitations (no full-text search).
2025-07-02 (Chloe Martin): Merged. Feature flag default off; enabled for internal orgs. Follow-up: add one integration test in ENG-2492 to assert audit events emitted for audit log read/export.
